summary: Apple's framework lets device-management vendors list and install institution-assigned apps, and it requires Apple's Managed App Installation UI entitlement. BifrOSt has a store install pipeline that it controls itself, but no device-management layer and no assigned-app list, so the framework has no counterpart.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/ota.rs (StoreApp plan from the store service)
features.note: The store plan is BifrOSt's own catalogue; there is no list assigned by a device-management server
Downloads and verifies sha256 and reports progress; there is no install-initiated check from a managing app and no launch-after-download hook
The store UI is the PC App Store app; it has no embeddable view for third-party management tools
Depends on the managed-offer model, which only exists with Apple's device management

features.apple: Managed App Installation UI entitlement, declarative management
features.note: BifrOSt has no device-management protocol; store packages cannot receive a management entitlement
Install errors are returned by the install code, not as a framework error set

gaps: No device-management server or declarative management protocol, so no institution-assigned app lists
No SDK API for a management tool to start or observe an install
Install progress is not exposed to apps (only the shell's update path uses it)
